cards.text: This is a Shiggaion that David, king of Israel (2 Samuel 5:3), sang to the LORD about the words of Cush, a Benjamite. The psalm never says what Cush said, and I am NOT about to make it up. David opens by taking refuge in the LORD and asking Him to save him from all his pursuers.

cards.question: David pictures his pursuers like a lion. What does he say they'll do to him if no one rescues him?
True or false: David says that if the LORD doesn't rescue him from his pursuers, someone else will.

cards.text: Then David puts himself on trial: if I have done this, if injustice is on my hands. That's like telling your boss, "Go ahead, PULL the security footage," and you only say that when you KNOW what's on the tape.

cards.question: David keeps going with his if-I-did-it list. True or false: one item on it is rewarding his ally with evil.
David says that if he really has done these things, what should happen to him?

answers.text: Let his enemy trample him down
Let the LORD forgive him anyway
Let the elders settle the matter

cards.text: Then David's if-I-did-it list is done, and he calls out: "Arise, O LORD, in Your anger; rise up against the fury of my enemies." No whispering in this prayer, friend. This is the LOUD part.

cards.question: With his enemies in a fury, David cries, "Awake, my God," and asks Him to do what?

cards.text: Now David paints a HUGE picture: the assembled peoples gathered around the LORD, and the LORD taking His seat over them on high. Every seat in the house is full, and believe me, nobody's checking their phone.

cards.question: With the peoples gathered around Him, David says the LORD ___ the peoples.
David asks the LORD to vindicate him. True or false: he asks for it according to his royal rank.

cards.text: David asks God to put an end to the evil of the wicked and establish the righteous. Down here, somebody can send a thumbs-up in the group chat while they're FUMING on the other end of that phone, but that doesn't work with this Judge.

cards.question: What does David say the righteous God searches?

cards.text: Next, David tells us where his protection is. Friend, when the pressure is on, you find out FAST who's really got your back.

cards.question: David says his shield is with ___, who saves the upright in heart.
David calls God a righteous judge. True or false: David says God feels indignation only once in a while.

cards.text: Then the picture turns sharp: God sharpening His sword, bending and stringing His bow, and ordaining His arrows with fire. Me? I've got an oven timer. That's my WHOLE arsenal.

cards.question: David says God will sharpen His sword. For whom?

cards.text: Now David turns the spotlight on the wicked man, and he uses a picture of pregnancy: the man travails with evil and conceives trouble. That one's been on the way for a WHILE, friend, and nobody is throwing it a shower.

cards.question: The wicked man conceives trouble. What does David say he gives birth to?

cards.text: The wicked man digs a hole and hollows it out. I bet he even stepped back to admire it.

cards.question: True or false: the wicked man ends up falling into the hole he dug.

cards.text: His trouble recoils on himself, and his violence falls on his own head. Friend, I spent YEARS stuck in a junk drawer I didn't even build, and this man DUG his!
After the swords, the arrows and the pit, David turns back to the LORD. He says he will "sing praise to the name of the LORD Most High."

cards.question: David also says he will thank the LORD for His ___.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the quoted call to arise, 'No whispering in this prayer, friend.' and 'This is the LOUD part.' It isn't the opening card, so the limit is two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question says 'if no one rescues him.' Card 3 asks whether David says someone else will rescue him, so card 2 has already given away card 3's answer (False). Card 3 also adds a condition the text doesn't have ('if the LORD doesn't rescue him'). Verse 7:2 just says 'with no one to rescue me.'

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The joke puts a modern image inside the Bible scene: 'every seat in the house is full' and 'nobody's checking their phone' describe the peoples gathered around the LORD. It isn't a separate everyday comparison.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The right answer 'Ordain judgment' is shorter than the wrong answers and sounds more like the Bible. The wrong answers ('Send rain on the land', 'Bless the king's army') are longer and plainer, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The card tells God sharpening His sword and stringing His bow as if it is simply happening. It drops the condition in verse 7:12, 'If one does not repent.' The text makes the sword-sharpening conditional.

The card asks the baker to finish the line 'he conceives trouble and births ___.' The wrong answers 'Regret' and 'Shame' are just as reasonable as 'Falsehood,' so the baker can only guess the wording.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
